transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-22 11:40 UTC | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Head of ML, Atlas), Marco Ruiz (Infra Eng), Lina Zhang (SRE)

Summary (auto): Deep dive on integrating OpenTelemetry with Redwood runtime to capture token-level metrics, tracing KV cache hits/misses, batching boundaries, and quantization impacts. Discussed cardinality concerns, span/metric naming, dashboards, and pilot next steps.

Topics: OpenTelemetry instrumentation, token-level metrics, OTLP collector config, Prometheus mapping, tracing through batching and KV cache, tagging for model/version/route, VPC/on-prem constraints, dashboards and alerts.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a technical deep dive focused on observability, OpenTelemetry and token-level metrics, Ethan will walk through examples. quick intro who we have?
[00:18] Priya: Hi this is Priya, head of ml at Atlas, focused on latency SLOs and being able to tie token cost back to features.
[00:25] Marco: Marco, infra, we'll own the networking and staging access, interested in cardinality and storage costs for metrics.
[00:33] Lina: Lina, SRE, we'll be on-call, want good alerting for KV cache thrash and sudden token cost spikes.
[00:40] Ethan: Great thanks, Ethan from Redwood infra team, i've been working on the runtime and the tracing hooks.

[01:02] Ethan: Quick agenda: show a demo trace, walk through instrumenting the runtime with OpenTelemetry, discuss token-level metric design, talk about batching boundaries and how spans are created per-request vs per-token, then dashboards and alert suggestions.
[01:18] Samira: One ask from you — show how this works in Dedicated and Private since Atlas might go dedicated or on-prem.

[02:05] Ethan: Ok starting with a sample trace — note this is a bit noisy since transcriber sometimes mashes names. But imagine an incoming request hits the router, then goes to the serving runtime where we may do prefix KV cache lookup, maybe a quantized runtine path, then streaming tokens back.
[02:25] [Demo noise — screen shares link: https://redwood.ai/docs/observability sample-otlp-config.pdf]
[02:40] Ethan: In our tracing model we emit spans at these logical boundaries: http_ingest -> route -> model_infer -> kv_lookup -> kv_hit or kv_miss -> tokenize -> decode_token -> emit_stream. For token-level visibility we create a lightweight metric per token event and also optional token spans when you need per-token latency distribution.
[03:08] Priya: Wait, per-token spans sounds expensive, do you sample those?
[03:14] Ethan: Yes we recommend sampling. Default approach: emit aggregated counters for token counts, token_latency_histogram with low-cardinality labels (model, route, quantization_profile) and then only emit detailed spans for 1 in N requests or for requests that hit some error or exceed lat SLOs.
[03:37] Marco: Cardinality is my worry — model+route+user_id+prompt_id explodes, how do you suggest we tag?
[03:45] Ethan: Keep tags minimal, we suggest: service=redwood-runtime, model, model_version, route (or api_key_product), hw_tier (e.g., a100, h100), quant_profile (int8,int4,fp16), and outcome (kv_hit/kv_miss). Avoid user_id at metric level; funnel per-request debug traces to a separate storage or use sampling export to a trace backend.
[04:12] Lina: For KV cache metrics, can we get hit ratio per-model and per-prefix?
[04:18] Ethan: Yes — we emit kv_cache_hits_total and kv_cache_misses_total with model/model_version/route labels. For prefix breakdowns we expose a limited set of prefix buckets (e.g., 64/256 length buckets) to avoid high-cardinality. Also we do a top-K prefixes export as a sampled trace event for debugging.
[04:40] Priya: How do you map OpenTelemetry -> Prometheus so our dashboards can use Prom?
[04:45] Ethan: Two patterns: 1) OTLP collector scrapes and converts to Prometheus remote write or using Prometheus receiver and a metric_relabeling rules to drop high-cardinality labels. 2) Redwood can push a Prometheus metrics endpoint from the runtime in Dedicated/Private. We'll share a config snippet. (link: https://redwood.ai/examples/otlp-prometheus-mapping)
[05:10] Ethan: Example metric naming we use: redwood_runtime_infer_duration_seconds_bucket, redwood_tokens_emitted_total, redwood_kv_cache_hits_total, redwood_kv_cache_miss_total, redwood_batch_size_distribution_seconds or histogram.
[05:30] Marco: For batching — are tokens emitted within a single span that covers the entire batch, or individual spans per request?
[05:38] Ethan: We model it as nested spans: a batch_spawn span with child inference spans per logical request. Token emission is a child event within the request span. That lets you compute queueing time (batch wait) vs GPU kernel time.
[05:55] Priya: And for quantization paths, do you tag spans for quant profile so we can A/B compare latencies?
[05:59] Ethan: Exactly — span/resource attributes include quant_profile. You can then filter traces for quant_profile=int8 and compare. We also emit a quantization_regret metric when output quality drops below eval thresholds (optional).
[06:18] Lina: Any examples of dashboards or alerts you recommend?
[06:22] Ethan: Yes — starter dashboards: 1) Token economics: tokens_emitted_total by route, cost_estimate per token; 2) Latency heatmap: infer_duration histogram by model_version and quant_profile; 3) KV cache health: hit_ratio over time and top prefixes; 4) Batching profile: batch_wait_seconds vs infer_seconds; 5) Error/bad-quality alerts: quant_regret_rate > threshold. We'll share Grafana JSON in the follow-up.
[07:00] Samira: A note for Dedicated/Private customers — network egress to OTLP collector might be restricted, so we provide a local collector config and instructions for on-prem OTLP forwarding.
[07:14] Marco: Good point, for compliance we need config that keeps PII out of traces. How do you handle redaction?
[07:20] Ethan: We support pre-export processors in the collector and runtime-level filtering. We never include full prompt text in metrics, only hashed prompt_id and optional truncated prompt tokens for debug spans (sampled). We'll provide sample config for attribute_processing to redact prompt content.
[07:44] Priya: Can you show an example trace for a slow request where kv_miss caused additional 100ms?
[07:50] Ethan: Sure — demo trace: [trace starts] http_ingest (2ms) -> batch_wait (35ms) -> kv_lookup (5ms) -> kv_miss (cache_miss path triggers recompute, +120ms) -> model_infer (90ms GPU) -> decode_stream (10ms) total 262ms. The trace has attributes: model=redwood-open-7b, quant_profile=int8, route=atlas-prod, outcome=kv_miss.
[08:25] [Transcription glitch: 'redwood-open' sometimes shows as 'red-wood open']
[08:40] Marco: On storage costs for metrics — if we export per-token metrics, that will blow up; what's your recommended aggregation window?
[08:49] Ethan: We recommend aggregated counters at the second granularity and histograms for latency with exemplars for problematic requests. Per-token counters should be aggregated per-request into tokens_emitted_total instead of one metric per token line. Token-level spans are sampled.
[09:10] Priya: We also want to attribute token cost to feature flags (some features add tokens). Do you suggest adding feature flag labels?
[09:18] Ethan: Add a low-cardinality feature_set label (e.g., ff=summary, ff=none, ff=search) but avoid enumerating every flag combination. Another pattern is to emit a taggable attribute for feature fingerprint and process offline join with cost data.
[09:35] Lina: How about alert thresholds — example SLOs we should set?
[09:40] Ethan: Suggested SLOs: 95th latency < 300ms for short prompts, kv_cache_hit_ratio > 85%, token_emitted_cost_per_1M < $X (depends on pricing). We can provide baselines from Redwood Dedicated runs.
[09:58] Priya: For on-prem, will the Collector live inside our VPC?
[10:02] Ethan: Yes. For Private customers we recommend running the OpenTelemetry Collector inside your VPC and forwarding via internal endpoints to your observability stack. Redwood runtime exposes an internal OTLP endpoint that the collector can scrape or you can push directly from runtime.
[10:20] Marco: What about tracer sampling config? We don't want to overflow our trace backend.
[10:25] Ethan: Typical config: parent_based always_on for errors, tail_sampling policy for traces that show high latency or kv_miss, plus probabilistic sampling 0.01 (1%) for general traffic. We'll share recommended collector.yaml.
[10:45] Samira: Quick comment on dashboards — we'll ship a Grafana pack for you to import and extend.

[11:00] Ethan: Now some concrete examples of metric names and labels: 
  - redwood_runtime_infer_duration_seconds_bucket{model="redwood-open-7b", model_version="v2", route="atlas-prod", quant_profile="int8"}
  - redwood_tokens_emitted_total{route="atlas-prod", model="redwood-open-7b"}
  - redwood_kv_cache_hits_total{model="redwood-open-7b", prefix_bucket="0-32"}
  - redwood_batch_wait_seconds_sum/count

[11:35] Priya: Can Redwood emit exemplars so we can link a Prometheus histogram bucket back to a trace?
[11:40] Ethan: Yes we support exemplars when using Prometheus remote_write with exemplars or using OpenTelemetry exemplars -> trace_id mapping. That requires keeping trace IDs for sampled traces and a push path to a tracing backend that supports exemplars.
[11:58] Marco: For quantization quality regressions you mentioned 'quant_regret' — how is that computed?
[12:04] Ethan: It's optional: during evals we compute ngram/embedding-based similarity against baseline; at runtime we run lightweight classifiers for hallucination or a small eval subset and if quality metric drops we emit quant_regret events tagged by model/version/quant_profile. It is heavier, so we sample or run it on a subset of traffic.
[12:27] Priya: Are there pre-built alerts for rollback if quant_regret spikes after a rollout?
[12:31] Ethan: Yes our rollout tooling ties into observability — you can set thresholds that automatically rollback to previous model or increase sample size. We'll show the A/B rollout example in the follow-up deck.

[13:05] Lina: A couple operational Qs: 1) How to debug when batch sizes suddenly increase? 2) How to correlate batch wait with upstream traffic surges?
[13:15] Ethan: For (1) use redwood_batch_size_distribution histogram and redwood_batch_wait_seconds to find correlation. For (2) instrument ingress (requests_per_second) and queue length metrics, then create a composite alert when batch_wait increases and ingress RPS changes.
[13:35] Priya: Any gotchas for private networks and on-prem hardware?
[13:40] Ethan: Latency from runtime -> collector must be low; we advise running collector local to runtime or on same host. Also ensure kernel params for high IO and set appropriate ulimits for the runtime. We'll share a checklist.

[14:05] Samira: Let's talk timeline for pilot — Ethan suggested a 2-4 week pilot where we run a subset of traffic on Dedicated, collect metrics and iterate. Does Atlas have a timeline?
[14:15] Priya: We're aiming to validate in Q2, so a pilot starting end of April into May works. We'll need security review and a short bench.
[14:25] Samira: Great we'll send security docs and the collector config today or tomorrow.

[14:40] Marco: Ok last thing — can we get an example collector config now in chat?
[14:45] Ethan: Yep, sending a gist in the chat, sample below (brief):

  receivers:
    otlp:
      protocols:
        grpc:
        http:
  processors:
    batch:
    attributes:
      actions:
        - key: prompt_text
          action: delete
  exporters:
    prometheus:
      endpoint: 0.0.0.0:9464
    otlp/remote:
      endpoint: <your-prometheus-remote-write>
  service:
    pipelines:
      metrics:
        receivers: [otlp]
        processors: [batch, attributes]
        exporters: [prometheus, otlp/remote]

[15:22] Priya: perfect thanks, we'll review.

[15:30] Samira: Ok wrapping up, recap next steps: Samira send security/pricing/docs, Ethan sends collector.yaml and Grafana pack, Atlas to provide sample traffic and grant staging access. We'll schedule the pilot kick-off.
[15:50] Priya: thanks all, this was useful.

[16:00] End of call: duration ~60 minutes
